Whispering Gallery
In an ellipsoidal room, sound waves radiating outward from focus F' bounce off the walls and converge at focus F.

plan.contextChunk: This figure is a shaded three-dimensional cutaway drawing of a domed room built as a half-ellipsoid on a circular base. The outer shell carries a blue-to-white gradient and is cut away at the front so the viewer looks into the interior, where the inner surface and the floor are shaded warm tan; a thick gray band forms the base slab beneath the floor. Two small dark points on the floor mark the foci, labeled F' on the left and F on the right. A fan of dark blue segments with arrowheads leaves F', rises at a range of angles to strike the inside of the curved dome at several separated points, and reflects back down, every one arriving at F. The paths cross one another mid-room, and no two share a bounce point. Drawing many distinct routes between the same pair of labeled points emphasizes that the convergence holds no matter which direction a ray sets out in. The illustration accounts for the acoustics of a whispering chamber, where a person speaking softly at one focus of an elliptical dome is heard clearly by a listener at the other.

elements: Base slab: thick dark gray elliptical cylinder beneath the floor
Floor: flat tan elliptical surface
Dome: semi-transparent blue half-ellipsoid covering the floor
Foci: two black dots on the major axis of the floor
Labels: 'F\'' on the left focus, 'F' on the right focus
Sound rays: 5 distinct dark blue polygonal lines with directional arrowheads, originating at F', striking the dome, and terminating at F
Sound pulses: small bright dots that travel along the rays during animation

interactions.teaches: Rotating the view reveals that the reflection property holds in all three dimensions of the ellipsoidal dome, not just in a flat plane.
Clicking an individual ray highlights its specific route, demonstrating that every launch angle leads to a valid reflection arriving at F.

interactions.label: Ray View
interactions.teaches: Switching from a single highlighted route to the full fan of paths shows that the focus-to-focus convergence is a systematic property of the entire surface.

interactions.label: Play Sound Pulses
interactions.teaches: Because every reflection path has exactly the same total length, sound waves leaving F' simultaneously will all arrive at F at the exact same moment, creating the acoustic concentration of a whispering gallery.

demo_steps.title: Individual Paths
demo_steps.narration: Isolating a single path shows the geometry of reflection. No matter where the ray hits the dome, its total travel distance remains constant.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: The dome is a half-prolate spheroid. Semi-major axis a=5 along X, semi-minor axes b=3 along Y and Z. Base floor is the XZ plane (Y=0). Foci are at X = ±4. Base floor tan #eeddcc, base rim gray #555555, dome transparent blue #4a90e2 with opacity 0.35. F' is (-4, 0, 0), F is (4, 0, 0). Generate 5 points on the dome surface (y > 0) to serve as bounce points for the rays, e.g., using x ∈ {-2.5, -1, 0, 1.5, 3} and varying z to distribute them in 3D, calculating y = 3 * sqrt(1 - x^2/25 - z^2/9). Rays are dark blue #003377.
interactionPlan.notes: When 'Single Ray' is active, fade out the unselected rays to a very low opacity. For the animation, ensure the pulses move at a constant linear speed so they arrive at F simultaneously, since the total path length (2a = 10) is identical for all paths.

plan.authoredInteractions:
- Click for an outgoing sound ray from F': the learner selects one path and its reflection point and return segment to F are highlighted, making clear that different launch angles still arrive at the other focus.
- Animation for sound propagation: the learner plays pulses leaving F', bouncing once off the ellipsoidal dome, and converging at F, making clear the dynamic reflection path behind the whispering-chamber effect.

authoredContext:
Many real-world situations can be represented by ellipses, including orbits of planets, satellites, moons and comets, and shapes of boat keels, rudders, and some airplane wings. A medical device called a lithotripter uses elliptical reflectors to break up kidney stones by generating sound waves. Some buildings, called whispering chambers, are designed with elliptical domes so that a person whispering at one focus can easily be heard by someone standing at the other focus. This occurs because of the acoustic properties of an ellipse. When a sound wave originates at one focus of a whispering chamber, the sound wave will be reflected off the elliptical dome and back to the other focus. See the figure. In the whisper chamber at the Museum of Science and Industry in Chicago, two people standing at the foci—about 43 feet apart—can hear each other whisper. When these chambers are placed in unexpected places, such as the ones inside Bush International Airport in Houston and Grand Central Terminal in New York City, they can induce surprised reactions among travelers.

Sound waves are reflected between foci in an elliptical room, called a whispering chamber.

An illustration of a semi-ellipsoidal dome with two focal points, F and F'. Blue lines with arrows represent rays originating from focal point F'. These rays reflect off the inner curved surface of the dome and converge at the second focal point F, demonstrating the reflective property of an ellipse.

discrepancies: F and F' labels are extremely tiny and practically unreadable
Arrowheads on the rays are bulky 3D cones instead of sleek directional arrows
Dome material appears grayish and slightly opaque instead of vibrant transparent blue
The base has a plain flat gray edge rather than the stylized rim seen in the source
evaluation.notes: The 3D geometry and underlying mathematical concept of the ellipsoid are perfectly executed with great interactivity, but the stylistic execution of the arrows and the legibility of the labels fall short.
action_items: Significantly increase the font size (e.g., 24px) and weight of the F and F' labels to ensure they are legible
Make the arrow cones on the rays much narrower (smaller radius) so they blend better as directional markers on the lines
Adjust the dome material properties (e.g., lower opacity, adjust color gradient) to achieve a clearer, more vibrant blue glassy look

feedback.rationale: The conceptual and geometric foundation is perfect, but the unreadable labels (score of 2) and minor styling issues with the arrows and materials require specific implementation fixes from the generator.

discrepancies: The ray arrowheads in the generated figure are much smaller than the prominent ones in the source figure.
The base in the source has a distinct raised rim and two-tone edge, whereas the generated figure has a simple flat cylinder.
The transparent dome in the source figure has a visible thickness/glass edge at the bottom, which is missing in the generated figure.
The labels F' and F are proportionally smaller in the generated figure compared to the source.
evaluation.notes: The generated figure accurately models the mathematics of the ellipsoid and its foci, along with excellent interactive features, though it lacks a few stylistic details of the source like the thick base rim.
action_items: Increase the size of the ConeGeometry used for the arrowheads to match the source figure.
Add a TorusGeometry or an outer hollow cylinder to simulate the raised rim of the base slab.
Increase the fontSize parameter for the F and F' labels to improve legibility.
